value.title: Doc procedures and worked examples for PRDs, blueprints and roadmaps
value.summary: Roadmap 001 step s13. The pij skill gets a short procedure and a worked example for writing a PRD, a blueprint and a roadmap under docs/project, and for folding a ruling into them, so a PM that has never seen PRD 001 can write linked, valid docs.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Delivers PRD 001 req-23 and starts c-skill (the `/pij community` route itself is s10, which links to these files). Sources: docs/project/README.md, docs/project/workshops/001-pij-community/002-limits-and-doc-prompting.md (points 6 to 8), the three schemas in .dd/schemas/pij/, and PRD 001, blueprint 001 and roadmap 001 as the live example. Also closes s01, which #108 merged but left in-progress.

sections.name: goals
value: A PM can write a PRD, a blueprint and a roadmap that validate and link, from one short procedure per type.
A PM can fold a ruling into existing docs without deleting rows.
The procedure says who writes: the PM that owns the work, with the prime helping; the prime itself when the operator asks.
Roadmap steps name the roles they need (`needs`), as workshop 002 point 8 says.

sections.name: non_goals
value: The `/pij community` route and its registry row (s10).
New schemas or schema changes. If the procedure exposes a schema gap, record it as a follow-up note to pm-001.

value.claim: Procedures. Files under skills/pij/references/community/ (one per doc type, plus folding a ruling) say, in plain steps: where the file goes and how to get its NNN (ask pm/001 until `pij claim` exists, s11); the ddocs commands to create, edit, validate and build it; how the link cells join roadmap steps to requirement rows and components; the state rules (a builder flips a row in the PR that delivers it; rows are amended, never deleted; drop with state dropped and a note); and `needs` on roadmap steps. Each file stays short enough to read in one pass.
Worked examples. A small linked example PRD, blueprint and roadmap ship beside the procedures and validate clean; the procedures point to them and to PRD 001 as the full-size example.

Fresh-PM canary. A seat with no prior context, given only the procedure and a short intent, writes a PRD and a roadmap in a scratch copy that validate clean and link to each other. Where it hesitated is fixed in the procedure, or recorded.

States. Before flipping, s01's done-when is checked and recorded. In this PR: roadmap s01 and s13 go to shipped (s13's plan cell set to docs/plans/191-doc-procedures); req-18 and req-23 go to shipped; c-doc-schemas goes to shipped; c-skill goes to in-progress. docs/project/README.md points at the procedures. All three project docs validate clean.

value.title: Procedures, examples and a fresh-PM canary
value.brief: AC1 to AC4. docs-system seat (pij-community-docs). CS-2.

value.approach: Validate the examples with ddocs; prove the procedure with a fresh canary seat.
value.rationale: The claim is that a newcomer can follow it, which only a newcomer can test.
value.excluded: Live governance and the prod daemon.

value.location: skills/pij/references/community/ and a pointer in docs/project/README.md.
value.rationale: s10's route will link here; until then the README is how a PM finds it.

value.question: Canary harness: OMP by default (AGENTS.md); docs-system may pick another if OMP is unavailable, and says which.

value.risk: The procedure grows into a manual nobody reads.
value.mitigation: Short files, one per type; the canary marks what was needed.
ddocs validate on the examples; harness checks covers them.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Never touch the prod daemon or the live governance branch.
Schema changes go back to pm-001 as a note, not into this PR.
